title:
Nonconvex Constraint Geometry: Set-Valued Projections,
Nonsmoothness, and Variational Structure under Manifold
Constraints
content: This paper develops a variational analysis of projected optimization over nonconvex constraint sets, with emphasis on the geometry and regularity of the metric projection. For a closed feasible set, the metric projection is treated as a set-valued mapping whose loss of local uniqueness may induce nonsmoothness and nonunique feasible continuations. Projection multiplicity and local projection regularity are related to the differentiability properties of the squared distance function, tangent-normal geometry, and first-order stationarity. These relationships provide a geometric characterization of regimes in which projected dynamics are locally single-valued or may branch. Smooth embedded manifolds arise as a locally regular case, where the existence of tubular neighborhoods ensures local uniqueness of the metric projection and the corresponding stationarity condition reduces to the vanishing of the Riemannian gradient. This framework, termed Nonconvex Constraint Geometry (NCG), connects set-valued projection, variational regularity, nonsmoothness, and manifold-constrained optimization within a unified geometric setting.
